    Reference study: nine doubly shadowed craters in Faustini, Haworth, and Shoemaker, plus Tooley. Positions plotted from Table 1 of the paper.

    F3~42%
    H3~10%

    Share of interior pixels with CPR above 1. F1, H2, S2, and S3 sit below 3%. H1 and Tooley show none.

    CPR > 1, DOP < 0.13

    ≤55 K

    Figures From the Paper

    Reproduced from Sinha et al. (2026), licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Non-commercial use with credit. Select a figure to enlarge it.

    F2

    Strongest Evidence

    Highest CPR share, low DOP, and a lobate rim. Impact point sits at −2,744 m, about 180 m below the surrounding floor. The raised rim is 20–25 m high.

    H3 · S1

    Partial Signals

    Elevated CPR in roughly 10% and 8% of interior pixels. Low DOP values match F2 and F3.

    Limits

    Radar Depth

    Radar reaches only a few meters. Ice buried deeper would not show, so no evidence is not proof of absence.

    Ice Verifier

    Computes CPR and DOP, applies the refined rule, ranks craters by ice confidence and terrain, plans a route, and writes a checkable report. Everything runs in your browser.

    1 · Pixel Check

    CPR
    —
    DOP
    —

    CPR = (σHH + σVV + 2√(σHH·σVV)) / (σHH + σVV − 2√(σHH·σVV)). DOP = √(S2² + S3² + S4²) / S1.

    Rule

    Strong
    CPR > 1 on ≥ 40% of pixels, DOP below threshold, lobate rim
    Likely
    Same, no lobate rim
    Partial
    3–40% of pixels, DOP below threshold
    None
    Under 3% of pixels, or DOP at or above threshold

    None means not detected in the top few meters. It never means no ice.

    2 · Validation Against the Paper

    …

    CraterCPR > 1 PixelsAvg DOPLobate RimTool RatingPaper RatingMatch

    The thresholds were set from these same ten craters, so a full match is a consistency check and not a test on new data. Inputs for F1, H2, S2, and S3 are given as “under 3%”; the paper gives no DOP for them.

    3 · Site Ranking & Route

    Score = 60% ice confidence + 20% gentle walls + 20% few boulders.

    Route Length
    —
    Drive Time
    —

    Straight-line legs between crater centers, nearest stop first. Real routes need terrain data.

    RankCraterRatingMax SlopeBouldersScoreRoute
